items.title: Allies press Israel to let winter shelter into Gaza
items.sub: 四國外長要求以色列放行 15 萬頂帳篷
items.summary: Foreign ministers from Australia, Canada, Italy and the UK issued a joint call for Israel to "stop the delays now" and allow roughly 150,000 tents and other winter relief supplies into Gaza before the cold season deepens. They said border restrictions are the main obstacle blocking shelter from reaching displaced families, and stressed the humanitarian crisis remains "entirely reversible" if crossings are opened. Aid agencies warn that flooding and low night temperatures are already affecting tented areas.

items.title: Third US carrier heads to Middle East as Iran tension builds
items.sub: 羅斯福號加入，美軍中東航艦增至三艘
items.summary: The New York Times reported the USS Theodore Roosevelt will join two other American carriers in the Middle East within a day, lifting the regional total to three. The move follows a second Iranian drone attack on Bahrain in three days. Iran's parliament speaker said Tehran will not accept a state of "neither war nor peace" and is ready for either negotiations or conflict, while warning any response to a new attack would not be limited or short-lived.

items.title: Tankers strike mines in the Strait of Hormuz, one sinks
items.sub: 荷莫茲海峽兩艘油輪觸雷、一艘沉沒
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said two oil tankers struck naval mines while transiting the southern Strait of Hormuz and that one of the vessels sank. The strait carries a large share of seaborne crude and any disruption there feeds quickly into freight insurance costs and global energy prices. The incident adds to a run of maritime security scares in the Gulf and raises the risk premium for shipping routes already under strain.

items.title: Estonia to shut all Russian border crossings from Dec. 1
items.sub: 愛沙尼亞 12/1 起關閉全部對俄口岸
items.summary: Estonia announced it will close every land border crossing with Russia starting December 1, after a failed sabotage attempt targeting an Estonian defence company. Separately, EU naval forces that boarded a suspected Russian tanker in the Mediterranean confirmed the ship was sailing under a false flag, according to Kaja Kallas. Both moves reflect hardening European policy toward Russia's shadow fleet and hybrid operations.

items.title: COP31 draft urges tripling adaptation finance to $120bn
items.sub: COP31 草案要求調適資金增至 1,200 億美元
items.summary: A draft decision at the Türkiye-hosted COP31 climate summit calls for tripling adaptation finance to about $120 billion and for accelerating the transition away from fossil fuels. President Erdogan described the summit as the "most successful to date." Negotiators still have to settle how the money is raised and delivered, and the fossil-fuel language remains one of the most contested parts of the text heading into the closing sessions.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet for agent payments
items.sub: ChatGPT 推出錢包，代理人可直接付款
items.summary: OpenAI rolled out ChatGPT Wallet, adding native payment execution so autonomous agents can complete shopping tasks end to end rather than handing users off to a checkout page. In a real-world commerce benchmark run by Visa, overall agent task completion reached 57.2%. Analysts note agent-driven sales volume is still small, and that merchant onboarding, disputes and returns remain unsolved operational problems before the format scales.

items.title: Cyberattack on La Poste unit exposes 22 million people
items.sub: 法國郵政子公司遭駭，2,200 萬人資料外洩
items.summary: A cyberattack on Maileva, the digital subsidiary of France's La Poste, reportedly exposed the personal data of roughly 22 million people. The breach is one of the largest disclosed in France this year and affects a service used to send digital and physical mail on behalf of businesses and public bodies. Investigators are still assessing which data categories were taken and whether credentials or financial records were included.

items.title: Thousands in Edinburgh protest large AI data centres
items.sub: 愛丁堡數千人上街反對 AI 資料中心
items.summary: Thousands of people marched in Edinburgh against plans for large-scale AI data centres in Scotland, citing power demand, water use and land impact. The protest is part of a widening pattern in which local opposition, rather than chip supply, is becoming the practical constraint on where AI compute gets built. Similar fights are under way in Ireland, the Netherlands and several US states where grid capacity is already tight.

items.title: Doncic pours in 43 as Lakers down the Suns
items.sub: 東契奇 43 分，湖人 131:123 擊敗太陽
items.summary: Luka Doncic scored a game-high 43 points to carry the Los Angeles Lakers past the Phoenix Suns 131-123. The Lakers controlled the game through long stretches of Doncic isolation offence and held on down the stretch as Phoenix pushed the pace. It was the standout individual line of the night across the league and extended a strong early-season scoring run for Doncic in his second year with the franchise.

items.title: Celtics crush Mavericks 131-94 behind Tatum's 32
items.sub: 塔圖姆 32 分，塞爾提克大勝獨行俠 37 分
items.summary: Jayson Tatum scored 32 points as the Boston Celtics dismantled the Dallas Mavericks 131-94 at home. Boston built the lead early and never allowed Dallas back within reach, with the bench extending the margin through the fourth quarter. The 37-point gap was the largest of the night and underlined Dallas's continuing problems containing opposing wings in transition.

items.title: Rockets post 147 points in rout of Wizards
items.sub: 火箭狂轟 147 分痛宰巫師
items.summary: The Houston Rockets scored 147 points in a 147-119 win over the Washington Wizards, the highest team total of the slate. Houston shot efficiently from distance and turned Washington's turnovers into easy transition baskets throughout. Elsewhere the New York Knicks edged the Toronto Raptors 112-108 in overtime, and the San Antonio Spurs beat the Utah Jazz 110-102 behind 31 points from rookie Dylan Harper.

items.title: Students using AI for emotional support report worse mental health
items.sub: 研究：向 AI 尋求情緒支持的學生心理狀態更差
items.summary: A new analysis reported by Education Week finds that students who turn to AI chatbots for emotional support report worse mental health outcomes than peers who do not. The data does not establish causation — struggling students may be more likely to seek any available outlet — but researchers warn that chatbot availability can delay contact with counsellors. Schools are being urged to pair AI literacy teaching with clear routes to human support.

items.title: Common ADHD classroom accommodations show no performance gain
items.sub: FIU 研究：常見 ADHD 課堂調整無助成績
items.summary: A Florida International University study found that the classroom accommodations most commonly granted to students with ADHD — such as extended time on tests — did not improve academic performance. The researchers argue that accommodations are often assigned by diagnosis rather than by the specific difficulty a student faces, and call for interventions that build skills, like organisation and homework-completion training, instead of simply extending deadlines.

items.title: College mental health improves but major gaps remain
items.sub: Healthy Minds：大學生心理健康改善但缺口仍大
items.summary: The latest Healthy Minds Study reports measurable improvement in college student mental health indicators, continuing a multi-year recovery from pandemic-era lows. Rates of reported depression and anxiety symptoms have edged down, yet a large share of students meeting criteria for a mental health problem still receive no treatment. Researchers point to counselling capacity and stigma as the two persistent bottlenecks on campuses.

items.title: Anthropic reportedly preparing ~$1tn-valuation IPO
items.sub: Anthropic 傳 11/19 掛牌，估值上看 1 兆美元
items.summary: Anthropic is reported to be preparing an IPO seeking to raise about $90.4 billion at a targeted valuation near $1 trillion, with a market debut slated for Thursday, November 19, 2026. Reported fundraising figures still vary across sources and remain subject to official filings. If it prices anywhere near that range it would be the largest technology listing on record and reset comparables for the entire frontier-model sector.

items.title: TSMC board approves minority stakes in OpenAI and Anthropic
items.sub: 台積電董事會通過投資 OpenAI 與 Anthropic
items.summary: TSMC formally disclosed a board resolution to acquire minority equity stakes in both OpenAI and Anthropic, with transaction values and ownership structures still under discussion. The move would tie the dominant foundry directly to its two largest frontier-model customers at a moment when advanced-node and CoWoS capacity allocation is the binding constraint on AI buildouts. Taiwan supply-chain names reacted strongly on the news.

items.title: Nvidia faces leadership turmoil ahead of Nov. 17 earnings
items.sub: 輝達人事動盪，11/17 財報登場
items.summary: A petition to reinstate Jensen Huang passed 150,000 signatures following his departure, and a robotics engineer resigned citing governance concerns. At the same time, US lawmakers are drafting tighter AI-chip export controls, including bills to curb foreign shipments and give Congress oversight of executive-branch approvals. Nvidia reports Q3 FY2027 results on November 17 against revenue guidance of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%.

items.title: YOASOBI releases new single "KILLA"
items.sub: YOASOBI 新曲〈KILLA〉數位上線，ツミキ 編曲
items.summary: YOASOBI digitally released the new song "KILLA," arranged by Tsumiki, along with its cover artwork. Live footage of the track from the ongoing "超惑星" tour was published at the same time. The release lands mid-tour and is the duo's first new material since the tour opened, with the arranger collaboration marking a noticeably harder-edged sound than their recent singles.

items.title: YOASOBI reshapes its Asia-Oceania tour lineup
items.sub: YOASOBI 亞洲巡演調整，部分城市取消、雪梨墨爾本加場
items.summary: YOASOBI announced a change to the title and routing of its 11-city Asia-Oceania tour 2026-2027, dropping shows in some countries and venues while adding Melbourne and Sydney dates. Fans holding tickets for affected cities are being directed to the official site for refund and exchange details. Taiwan and Hong Kong fans should check the official schedule page before buying flights or accommodation.

items.title: Kenshi Yonezu brings GHOST tour to Taipei Dome
items.sub: 米津玄師 12/26–27 台北大巨蛋開唱
items.summary: Kenshi Yonezu's 2026-2027 WORLD TOUR / GHOST includes two nights at Taipei Dome on December 26 and 27, with doors at 15:00 and showtime at 18:00. The Japanese leg continues this week with Osaka-jo Hall on November 18 and 19 before Fukuoka and Miyagi dates in December. Taiwanese fans should watch the local promoter's page for the on-sale window.

items.title: Vaundy wraps Taipei Arena shows on HORO Asia tour
items.sub: Vaundy 台北小巨蛋 HORO 亞洲巡演落幕
items.summary: Vaundy played Taipei Arena on October 31 and November 1 as part of the ASIA ARENA TOUR 2026 "HORO." The Taipei run was among the larger overseas stops on the tour and sold through quickly. With the Taiwan dates now finished, the remaining schedule moves on to other Asian cities, and no additional Taipei date has been announced.
